text:
Damon Severson plays 22 minutes a night for Columbus and is one of the most quietly effective defensemen in the league by Evolving-Hockey's numbers: 20th among 215 defensemen last season, 94th percentile for driving play and 96th for taking chances away. That is a rare combination.

This season's points come with help. He has nine in 19 games, but Columbus has scored about 9.3 more goals than its chances with him on the ice, which is a lot of luck and won't last. The underlying play is solid: the Blue Jackets are about three points better on five-on-five expected goals with him on than without (expected goals measure the quality of chances), on a team that is under water most nights. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him in the 88th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists. He spent 647 games in New Jersey before Columbus, and he faces his old team tonight. Our range has him around 36 points.
